The premise

Thousands of years after the first interplanetary war, a century of shifting alliances has left about one in ten of the old populations alive, and food production was among the first things the militaries targeted. Demand now runs far ahead of supply, so growers are being recruited. You are one of them: you pick a planet, take over a plot of land, and run it remotely through a tracked robot called the Farmoton.

You make money (nibs) by growing crops and selling them to the traders who dock at the planet's space port each day. Some crops are illegal and pay far more, but each alliance bans different ones, its inspectors fine you for them, and three strikes with an alliance get you banned from all its planets. You start with 2,500 nibs. Your first farm also comes with 5 seeds of the legal crop that suits it best (on most starting planets a perfect fit), in its seed shed, and the Farmoton tooling to plant them; you still need a trailer to harvest them and the right shed to store the harvest. The game ends only if you have no farm left and cannot afford a new one (the cheapest planet costs 300 nibs).

A new game plays the opening story, then planet selection; Watch Intro on the main menu plays the story again whenever you like, without starting a game. The Tipoton, a small robot that drives along the bottom-left of the screen, introduces itself before its first tip and then explains each screen and menu tab the first time you open it. Each tip shows once; Show tips again in the pause menu brings them all back.
Download the game from github.com/SmarterCircuits/InterplanetaryFarmerBeta/releases. Enjoying it? You can support its development with a donation at ko-fi.com/smartercircuits.

Days, time and the night

Each day starts at 6:00. On the farm screen one in-game hour takes 25 real seconds; the clock stops while any menu, report or visitor is on screen. The speed button beside the clock (or G) runs the farm at 1×, 2×, 3×: time, robots and animals all speed up together, so they get the same work done per in-game hour. Menus, visitors and puzzles always run at normal speed. Sunrise and sunset sit evenly around noon: sunrise = 12 − daylight ÷ 2.

When the clock passes midnight, or you end the day yourself, the night runs on every farm you own:

  1. Plants grow (or wither), and ripe single-harvest crops start to rot.
  2. Pests spread, weeds age, sprout and spread.
  3. The soil dries out.
  4. Inspectors may visit.
  5. Loan interest is added once, for all farms.
  6. The next day's weather and traders are rolled, and the game autosaves.

You choose how the Farmoton spends the night:

Ending the dayBatteryWear
Park in the garage (face the garage and press Space, or press N while beside it)Topped up by the charger, at the garage's priceRepaired (maintenance), and no weather exposure
End Day (N) or let midnight passOnly the rest of today's sunlightNo repairs, and harsh weather adds wear

A farm report follows each night. It has a foldable section per farm: the farm you are on and the morning outlook start open, your other farms start folded, and a folded section shows ⚠ when it holds a warning. Long reports scroll. Tick Auto-continue beside the Continue button and reports close themselves after 5 seconds, so the game can run unattended; the setting is saved with your game. Visiting robots then answer themselves too when they only have news for you, but an offer or request that needs your decision still waits for you.

The Farmoton

The Farmoton is one tile in size. It always works on the tile directly in front of it, outlined in yellow. Tapping a direction turns it on the spot; holding the direction drives it forward one tile at a time (about 0.3 s per tile with stock motors). Buildings and weeds block it, and so do helper robots.

Tools

KeyToolEnergyWhat it does
1Plow3Turns a plot tile so a seed can go in. A planted or growing tile must be cut first.
2Plant1Plants the selected seed from the hopper on a plowed, empty tile.
3Water1Pours 4 water from the onboard tank, adding 45 moisture to the tile (max 100).
4Cut down2Clears a weed anywhere, or cuts down a plant (alive or dead), leaving the soil plowed.
5Harvest2Picks a ripe plant into the trailer. Needs a trailer with room for the whole yield, and the crop's tooling.
6Spray1.5Uses one dose of pesticide to clear pests from a tile. Needs the Pest Sprayer tooling.
7Move3Picks up the building ahead; press again to put it down (putting down is free).

Facing a building and pressing Space uses the building instead: the water tank fills the onboard tank, the seed shed swaps the hopper's contents for the selected seed, a crop shed unloads matching goods from the trailer, and the garage parks for the night.

Energy, solar charging and wear

  • Driving one tile costs 0.4 energy; each tool costs the amount in the table. Turning is free.
  • The solar panels charge the battery during daylight: charge per hour = solar rating × the planet's sun power.
  • Every move adds 0.025% wear and every action 0.125%. Wear makes everything cost more energy: energy × (1 + wear ÷ 100), so 30% wear means 30% more energy per job.
  • A night outside adds exposure wear when the weather is outside 5–28°C or 25–75% humidity: 0.4% per degree outside the range + 0.15% per humidity point outside it (ignored below 0.5%). Helpers take the same exposure.
  • Maintenance in the garage costs 1.5 nibs per 1% of wear and repairs as much as you can pay for.

Each planet has one soil type. Without tracks for it, every move onto a plot tile takes 3× as long and uses 3× the energy. Tracks, like all parts, belong to that farm's Farmoton.

Planets

There are 57 planets, each named after a real star or body and a kind of land. A farm costs between 300 and 650 nibs. Every planet has fixed traits and a yearly cycle:

Sun color
0 is a red sun, 0.5 white, 1 blue. It tints the farm's light, and crops prefer a particular color.
Sun power
Multiplies how fast solar panels charge.
Temperature and daylight
Follow a sine wave over the planet's year: value = average + swing × sin(2π × day-of-year ÷ year length).
Seasons
Each year splits into four equal seasons: Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter.
Humidity
Constant all year.
Rain
Each morning it rains with the planet's rain chance. See Water.
Water price
Nibs per unit to refill the farm tank at the market.
Pests
The planet's pest and its nightly chance per plant. Some planets have none.
Inspections
A strictness multiplier on inspections, stings and fines. Lower strictness also brings more smugglers.
Alliance
The alliance the planet belongs to. See Alliances.

Crops and growth

There are 30 crops in eight categories. A category decides which shed stores the harvest and which tooling plants and picks it. A ninth category, Animal Goods, holds the materials animals make.

Suitability

Each crop prefers a sun color, hours of daylight, temperature, humidity and soil. Every factor scores from 0 to 1, and suitability = light × daylight × temperature × humidity × soil.

FactorFull score withinScore falls to 0 at
Light (sun color)± 0.25± 0.5
Daylight± 3 h± 6 h
Temperature± 7 °C± 14 °C
Humidity± 18 %± 36 %

Soil scores 1 on the crop's best soil, 0.6 on its second soil and 0.15 on anything else. The HUD shows the selected seed's score for today, factor by factor.

Growing each night

Plants go through five stages: planted seed → seedling → sprout → plant (ripe) → dead plant. Each night a living plant gains

growth = suitability × water factor × weed factor ÷ days per stage

  • Water factor is 1 if the tile's moisture meets the crop's need (low 20, medium 40, high 60), otherwise 0.25.
  • Weed factor is 0.5 if a weed grows on the tile, otherwise 1.
  • Each full point of growth advances one stage, so in ideal conditions a crop ripens in 3 × its days per stage.
  • Infested plants do not grow at all.
  • If the night's rate (before dividing) is below 0.2, the plant is stressed. After 4 stressed nights in a row it dies.
  • A ripe single-harvest crop rots and dies after 5 nights unpicked. Regrowing crops wait indefinitely.

Harvest and yield

Every night's growth rate is averaged into the plant's quality.

units harvested = round(yield × (0.4 + 0.6 × quality)), at least 1

Regrowing crops (trees, bushes, beans) go back to a sprout after picking and lose 0.5 of a stage. Single-harvest crops become dead plants that you cut down before replanting.

Light: preferred sun color (0 red, 1 blue). Water need shows the moisture the tile needs. Harvest value is yield × base price in ideal conditions.

Water, rain and soil moisture

  • Every plot tile has moisture from 0 to 100. Watering adds 45, using 4 units from the Farmoton's onboard tank, which you fill at the farm tank.
  • The farm tank holds 200 / 400 / 700 units by level and is refilled at the market for the planet's water price per unit.
  • Rain: on a rainy morning every tile gains 50 moisture and the tank gains 60. While it keeps raining, tiles gain 12 per hour and the tank 5 per hour.
  • Evaporation overnight: clamp(14 + (temp − 15) × 0.8, 6, 40) × (1.2 − humidity ÷ 125). Hot, dry planets lose the most.
  • Thirsty plants show a blue drop on their tile.

Weeds and pests

Weeds

  • A new farm starts with 8 weeds. Each night each of the map's 496 cells has a 0.8% chance to start a new weed (in the grass only, about four a night).
  • Weeds age each night. From age 2 a weed spreads to each free neighbor with 2.5% chance, plot tiles included.
  • Weeds stop spreading once they cover 25% of the map (124 cells).
  • Weeds block robots, halve the growth of a plant sharing their tile, and raise pest odds. Cut them down (tool 4).

Pests

Each night every healthy plant on a planet with pests may be infested. Its odds are

planet pest chance × (1 + 0.04 × weeds on the farm) + 0.03 for a weed on or beside it (each) + 0.2 per infested neighbor

Infested plants stop growing and die after 5 nights. Spraying clears them; pesticide costs 4 nibs a dose at the market and one dose clears one tile.

The farm and its buildings

A new farm has a 5 × 5 plot, a water tank, a seed shed and its own stock Farmoton. The map is 41 × 16 tiles (taller as the plot grows) and scrolls as you drive. Buildings stand along the top and are each two tiles wide, except the big ones below. Upgrades are bought in the space port: the Local Builders handle Land (the plot), Village (amenities), Utility (water tank, garage, barn and relay) and Storage (sheds and the Food Warehouse); the Mining Union handles Mining; and the Roboton Dealer's Roboton Service counter upgrades the Farmoton and the helper Robots.

  • Sheds: the seed shed has no limit. Every other crop category needs its own shed before its harvest can be stored; see the category table. The Local Builders in the space port build them.
  • Food Warehouse (Upgrades → Storage): a 2×2-tile shed, one shed wide and two deep, that stores 2,500 goods of any food, produce included, on top of the crop sheds. Goods go in their own shed first; whatever it has no room for (or has no shed built) goes in the warehouse, and you can unload any harvest there. It has no upgrades and is too big to move, and it goes up wherever there's room off the plot.
  • Garage: park in it to sleep with charging and maintenance. Standing beside it charges the battery at 2× the solar panels' full-sun rate, for 1 nib per 1% of battery (the same price applies overnight).
  • Moving buildings: the Move tool (7) picks one up for 3 energy and puts it down free. Sheds must be empty first. The plot cannot grow over a building, so move it out of the way first.
  • Animal Barn and Produce Shed: the barn houses your animals; the Produce Shed (a crop-style shed) stores the materials they make.
  • Selling the Farmoton (Upgrades → Farmoton): 1,000 nibs, whatever its upgrades. You then work that farm on foot as a colonist: no battery, wear or breakdowns, any soil and crop, but slower, carrying a few seeds, a little water and a small basket, picking pests off by hand and unable to move buildings, and a manager has nothing to drive. A new stock Farmoton costs 3,000 nibs, or you can rent a top-spec one (every part at level 3, all tracks and tooling): 1 day for 50 nibs, 3 days for 150 nibs, 5 days for 250 nibs. It's collected at midnight on the rental's last day, and what it carried goes back to the farm. Buy or rent one from the Roboton Dealer in the space port.
  • Utility Shack and your air: every farm has a one-tile Utility Shack near where you start. Use it to go inside, a 12×12 room with an oxygen filling station and Swap-n-Match and Moon Maze cabinets to play while your tank fills, and walk out through its doorway to leave; it can't be moved. On foot, ending the day (N) sends you to sleep in the shack: you wake inside it in the morning, with the night's report, and step out beside its door. Inside the shack, N (or Sleep) does the same, and your tank fills for every hour you sleep. N also sleeps until morning in your Personal Space Base and the Void Yacht, where the tank fills only if the base has its oxygen filling station, and you're back where you left the farm. On foot (no Farmoton, and there in person rather than through the Command Center Chair) you breathe from an oxygen tank holding 60, shown by an air meter on the top bar. Walking and working use 60% of the air they would battery, and just breathing uses 0.6 an hour. When it runs out you're sent to refill it: to your Personal Space Base if you've bought its oxygen filling station (50,000 nibs in the Base Store), otherwise to the farm's utility shack. While you're in a building with a station, your tank fills on its own at 20 an hour at the farm's pace, half the speed a stock Farmoton charges beside the garage. The station makes its own oxygen: it's free and never runs out.
  • Remote Relay Station: see Other planets.
  • Refrigerated Warehouse: if you take Robototon Corporation's produce program (see Alliances), it replaces every crop shed on that farm, goods and all, and stores 5,000 goods of every kind. It belongs to Robototon, so it can't be moved, sold or upgraded, and no crop sheds can be built beside it.
  • Selling buildings: an empty shed, the garage, the barn (once its animals are sold) or the relay sells for 75% of what was spent on it, including upgrades. The seed shed cannot be sold.

Mining

Under every farm there's rock worth digging. Buy the farm's mineral rights for 50,000 nibs from the Planet Representative in the space port's Government House, and the Mining Union can set up the rest. Then:

  1. Hire an engineer: a local who costs 1,000 nibs up front and 100 nibs every 10 days, and moves into an Engineer's House in the village like the other workers. During their shift they survey for the mine and then inspect it from beside the entrance; off shift they have free time like everyone else. If the engineer quits for any reason or you let them go, the mine shuts at once: nobody goes down and the drone stops until you hire another. They have a mood like the farm hands and quit if unhappy for too long or if you can't pay them.
  2. Build the mine entrance (25,000 nibs). The engineer walks the farm for about 4 hours of their shift, then sinks a one-tile entrance at a random spot that's off the plot (as big as it can grow) and out of the village. A spot is kept for the Mineral Storage beside it; buildings that would have gone there go to the next free space.
  3. Buy a mining drone (15,000 nibs). It hovers like the Manager Robot, and down the mine you are the drone.
  4. Build the Mineral Storage (10,000 nibs): a 2×2-tile shed (the Food Warehouse's size) one tile from the entrance that holds 1,000 minerals. Ore you dig goes there; without room for it, ore can't be dug. Sell minerals to the ore buyer in the Mining tab.

Down the mine

Face the entrance and press Space to go down, the same way you go into the utility shack. Down there you are the drone. The mine is 20 floors deep, each a maze of tunnels in the dark. Fly with the movement keys, and over (or facing) a hatch press Space to go up or down a floor (the first floor's up hatch, or Esc, takes you back to the farm). Each floor starts as a small cave inside a 15×15 square; everything around it is rock. Hold Space facing a wall to laser it: it glows redder and redder, and after a few seconds it bursts and becomes floor, and if it was ore the ore goes to the Mineral Storage. Let go or turn away and the wall starts over. Outside that first square only the veins can be dug, winding bands through solid bedrock (the darkest walls), which nothing digs through. No floor reaches more than 120 tiles from its up hatch, so each is very large but not endless.

The drone's battery holds 8 hours of work, shown on the mine's top bar. It runs down as time passes while you're in the mine, and charges whenever you're out of it, at 30 minutes of work for every hour, so a flat battery takes 16 hours to fill. If it runs out while you're mining, it flies you straight back up to the farm and tells you why. You can't go down again until it has some charge.

The drone only digs while you fly it; it never mines on its own. Digging takes 3 s plus 0.5 s per point of hardness, and 15% less for every drone level above the one needed.

Animals

Alien livestock live in the Animal Barn and wander the grass by day (they never block the robots). Buy them, and Animal Feed at 2 nibs a unit, from the farming vendor in the space port's market. An animal sells back for 50% of its price.

Each night

  1. Eating: foragers find their own food first and only eat Animal Feed when there is none; the rest eat one unit of feed. An animal that doesn't eat makes nothing that night, and after 3 hungry nights in a row it wanders off for good.
  2. Its job, if it ate (Fluffwings pollinate whenever they are on the farm).
  3. Its material: each fed night adds its comfort (0–1) toward the next batch; a batch is made once the total reaches the nights in the table. Comfort scores temperature and humidity like a crop's suitability: full within the tolerance, falling to nothing at twice it. Batches go to the Produce Shed; with no shed, or no room, they spoil.

The beach and fishing

Every farm has a beach down a boardwalk from its bottom left corner: drive (or walk) into that corner and keep going down. Its sand and water depend on the planet's soil: olive mud on goo worlds, golden sand on loamy worlds, grey shingle on rocky worlds, rust-red sand on sandy worlds. Walk out along the pier and face the fishing boat tied up at its end, then press Space to get in. In the boat the movement keys row it a tile at a time (it turns first, as walking does), and Space casts the lure up to 3 tiles ahead into open water. Back beside the pier, Space ties the boat up and puts you on the pier. Time runs and your air runs down here as in the space port.

Under the water

Once the lure lands you see it from the side, swimming to the right. Left or A slows it and right or D speeds it up (it keeps the speed you leave it at); up or W and down or S move it while held, and it sinks slowly when left alone. Esc reels it back in. The water is shallow by the shore and deepest about 7 tiles out, and some fish keep to the depths.

Every kind of fish likes the lure moved its own way, and judges it by how it has moved over the last 5 seconds: how fast it swims, how much of the time it is bobbing up or down, how steady or changeable its speed is, how even or erratic its strokes are, and for some kinds a run of strokes, such as two ups and a down. A fish that likes what it sees comes closer, with a ? over it, and follows the lure; keep it up and it bites: a ! shows over it and the lure tugs. Press X quickly to hook it; wait too long and it lets go and swims off. If it stops liking the lure before it bites, it swims off and ignores the lure for a while. Bigger fish are more patient to win over.

Your catch

Fish you catch stay with you until you sell them to the farming vendor in the space port's market (heavier ones fetch more), or, for the kinds marked below, put them in your Personal Space Base's aquarium from its side panel. The inventory's Farm Storage tab lists your catch and every kind you've caught.

Markets, traders and money

The space port

Every planet has a small town up a path from the farm's top left corner: drive (or walk) into that corner and keep going up. Each planet's port is laid out differently and has its own residents, who keep routines of their own: they sleep and relax at home, go out walking (some with a pet), and run errands in the businesses that are open. Face one and press Space to chat: they talk about the planet and what they think of things, from the alliances to Roboton to each other. (Your farm hands chat the same way on the farm.) Walk in at a door to go inside, and face the staff behind each counter and press Space. Businesses keep hours, shown on the sign when they're closed: the Government House and the Bank 09:00–17:00, the Planet Hopper Dealer 10:00–20:00, the Local Builders 07:00–18:00 and the Mining Union 06:00–22:00. At closing time you're shown out. The market and the Roboton Dealer never close; their clerks work in shifts.

  • Market: the trading terminal sells to the traders docked today; the seed vendor sells seeds at each crop's seed price (they go to the seed shed; seeds illegal here are not sold); supply deliveries refill the farm water tank and sell pesticide; the farming vendor sells animals and feed.
  • Bank: the banker handles your loan. Roboton Dealer: the dealer sells helper robots, the Manager Robot and Farmotons to buy or rent, and the Roboton Service counter sells every Farmoton and helper upgrade. Planet Hopper Dealer: the Planet Hopper. Local Builders and the Mining Union: the farm's buildings and its mine (land, village, utilities, storage and mining).
  • IGA Office: Floop of the Interplanetary Growers Alliance. Once you own five farms she invites you to join: 10,000 nibs, then 1,000 every 30 days (you're asked before each renewal). Members are given Sklurbb, a personal assistant who pops up wherever you are with news of the alliances as it happens, keeps your aquarium's fish fed, and asks what you'd like to do when it matters to your farms. If your membership ends you can keep him on for 50 nibs every 10 days, or hire him back here later. Without him the news doesn't reach you, though when an alliance takes a planet you farm on, its officer will still come to ask what's needed.
  • When a planet you farm on changes hands, its new holder decides what to do with your farm, going by what you've done for both alliances: it may leave you be, offer to buy the farm, or take it, with or without paying. You're told a day ahead. Crops the new holder's laws ban must be given up or hidden (and hidden crops may be found).
  • Government House: the Planet Representative, who also sells the farm's mineral rights, and buys ore from your Mineral Storage for the planet's alliance (at three quarters of the Mining Union's price), or takes it as a gift; either pleases the alliance, a gift most of all. Ore sold at the Mining Union pleases the planet's people a little. Deliver the crops on the Liaisonoton's request once you have agreed to supply the planet (see Visiting robots). Every so often the planet also appeals here for a donation of 100–1,000 nibs; giving is up to you, but the people remember who helped. Its food drive takes everything in your sheds (contraband stays) as a gift to the planet's people: an easy way to clear out full sheds, and they think better of you for it. The Representative is also who you hire up to 10 farm hands, local colonists and the planet's own people. Each lives in a one-tile house in a village of workers' homes that starts in the farm's upper right corner (150 nibs to build, kept if they leave) and is paid 50 nibs when hired and every 10 days; one you can't pay quits. Choose each one's task there (any task a helper robot can do). They are slower than helper robots, work a shift of 8–10 hours a day starting between 7:00 and 9:00, and pick pests off by hand without pesticide. They keep working while you are away. Give them their tasks in the Helpers menu (H). The planet's people like it when you hire them, and dislike it on any day you spray pesticide.
    Workers take 2 hours off for lunch in the middle of each shift and have lives of their own off shift. They go to bed at night for 7–8 hours, and with time to spare they visit the amenities you've built, stroll about, stop to chat with each other and pet the farm's animals. Some own a pet, a little jelly goat in one of several colors, which they walk, take to the park and walk at lunch, before eating at the restaurant if the farm has one (otherwise at home). What they're thinking pops up now and then in a bubble over their heads, and a sleepy one floats over the house of anyone asleep. The Helpers menu shows when each sleeps and their pet.
    Each hand and your farm manager has a mood. Some mornings one asks for the day off (give it and they stay home and like you more; refuse and they like you less), and every 90 days worked you're asked whether to pay them a 100-nib bonus. Moods drift each night toward a resting level that each amenity you build raises (the library, mini-mall, park, recreation center, restaurant, theater, under Upgrades → Village). Someone left unhappy for too long quits ("Fed up" is the last warning), which upsets the planet, though less than letting them go.
    Keep a farm's whole staff happy for a long stretch and they pull together to thank you: first with the Admirable Humanoidatarian award for your awards case, then with furniture for your Personal Space Base. But a worker who stays unhappy may sneak in and steal that award back. Some hands are happier with a helper robot on the harvest, and none of them like working under a Manager Robot. A happy staff may also catch locals trying to steal your animals or set fire to your buildings.

Traders

Each morning 1–3 traders dock. Each buys 2–4 crop categories at 0.9×–1.8× base price, and has room for 20–60 units that day. Sales draw from the sheds first, then the Farmoton's trailer, then each helper's trailer.

Smugglers and illegal crops

  • Each trader is a smuggler with chance clamp(0.3 ÷ strictness, 10%, 70%), so lax planets attract more.
  • A crop is illegal on a planet if the planet's alliance bans it (the table below); it is legal everywhere else, where ordinary traders buy it and the market sells its seeds.
  • Smugglers also buy crops illegal on their planet at 1×–1.5× base price.
  • 60% of smugglers sell 1–3 kinds of seed illegal there, 5–20 of each, at 1×–1.6× the seed price.
  • Stings: each sale of contraband has a 8% × strictness chance that the buyer is an undercover inspector.

Enceladus PactRotatip, Wyvern Fruit, Mercurian Tamarind, Bulovian Cherry

Inspections, fines and strikes

Every farm you own may be inspected each night:

chance = 6% × strictness + min(35%, 1.5% × illegal items) × strictness

Illegal items are every living plant the planet's alliance bans plus every unit of banned goods or seeds in the sheds, robots and the Planet Hopper (so cargo legal where you loaded it can be illegal where you land). If anything illegal is found (or a sting catches you), it is all confiscated and you are fined

fine = 250 + 2 × value of the illegal items

and receive a strike with the planet's alliance. At 3 strikes with one alliance it bans you from all its planets for good: every farm you have on them is forfeited and you can't start a farm on them again. A farm is also seized at once if you cannot pay the fine.

Loans

  • Credit limit = 800 + 400 per plot expansion across all your farms, plus a good-standing bonus: +50 for every 14 nights in a row you owe nothing. A loan resets that count, which starts again once the loan is paid off; rises already earned stay.
  • Interest of 2% is added every midnight.
  • If the debt passes 2× the credit limit, the lender repossesses the farm you are on.
  • Losing a farm moves you to another one you own. With none left, the lender takes what it is owed from your savings.

Helper robots and the Manager Robot

Helpers

A helper is an automated Farmoton that works one task at a time: Water, Weed, Pest control, Harvest or Plant. Weed and Pest control also clear dead plants. A farm can have 5, costing 2,500, 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 40,000 nibs in turn.

  • Helpers are slower than you (0.6 s a tile, 1.4 s a job) but use only 25% of the energy and wear.
  • They fetch their own water, seeds and pesticide, carry their own trailer, and need their own tracks, tooling and parts (the Roboton Service counter). They wait above the plot when there is nothing to do.
  • A Brain Chip (1,500 nibs) gives a helper a backup task for whenever its main task has no work.
  • Sell a helper you no longer need from the Robot Help tab of the Helpers menu (H), for 75% of the latest helper's price and of what you spent upgrading it. The next helper is then cheaper again.
  • They are repaired and charged when you park in the garage, and take weather wear when you don't.

Everyone working the farm is set up in the Helpers menu (H), with a tab each for Robot Help, the Robot Manager, Farm Hands and the Farm Manager.

The Manager Robot

A small hovering robot for 20,000 nibs. It is the farm's autopilot, and can be sold back for 75% of its price from the Robot Manager tab of the Helpers menu. A farm has one manager: this robot, or a Farm Manager hired from the Planet Representative in the space port, who does everything below but only during a shift of 8–10 hours a day, steering the Farmoton by remote control from beside their house. A Farm Manager is paid 300 nibs when hired and every 10 days, and lives in a house like the farm hands.

  • Autopilot: it drives the Farmoton through every task no helper covers (as main or Brain Chip task), most urgent first: Pest control, Water, Harvest, Weed, Plant. Driving or using a tool switches the Farmoton to manual; P hands it back.
  • Planting: it plants the seeds ticked in its list, choosing the one that suits today best. With Next available on, it also plants any legal seed you have in stock, best suited first (it still only buys the ticked ones). Helper robots and farm hands have a Next available choice for their seed too.
  • Restocking (each can be switched off): water when the tank drops below 30%; pesticide up to 10 doses when under 3, if a robot there has the sprayer; each chosen legal seed the Farmoton has tooling for, up to 20 when fewer than 5 are left. It never spends below the reserve you set (0, 250, 1,000, 2,500, 5,000 nibs; default 1,000).
  • Animal Feed (can be switched off): keeps 6 nights of feed for the farm's animals, topping up below half of that.
  • Sell mode (off by default): sells shed goods to the day's traders, each unit to the best offer. It never sells contraband. If you have agreed to supply the planet, it first delivers what the Liaisonoton's request still needs (filling a request and then the next), and only sells what is left over. Money made on farms you are away from goes straight to your savings; the night report gives the total near the top.
  • Surplus (Manual by default): Sell to the Surplusoton sells it every legal good in the sheds and trailers whenever it comes; Donate leftovers delivers the planet's request and sells to the traders each night, as sell mode does, then gives the rest of the sheds' legal goods to the planet's food drive, keeping whatever the planet's request still needs.
  • Approve days off (off by default): the manager gives workers the day off when they ask, instead of asking you.
  • Garage nights: on autopilot with a garage, every 3 nights it parks the Farmoton for charging and repairs.
  • Away from the farm: a farm with a manager keeps working while you are elsewhere. Its helpers and (on autopilot) its Farmoton work from morning to midnight. Farms without a manager only grow, charge from the sun and catch the rain.
  • Its purchases, sales and garage nights appear in the nightly report.

Other planets and space stations

The Planet Hopper (8,000 nibs) flies between planets (T). Flying takes the night: the day ends with the Farmoton left outside, every farm has its night, and you land at dawn.

The travel menu's Map tab is a star chart of every planet and space station: the Sol system on the left, with moons grouped around their giant planets, and the worlds of other stars on the right, each beside its sun. Drag it or use the scroll wheel (Shift+wheel scrolls sideways). Your farms are ringed in green and where you are in gold. Show alliances draws lines in each alliance's color between its planets, with a key in the lower left corner; a dashed line reaches a member far away. Click a planet or station to see its details on the right (soil, today's weather, pests, inspections, the crops that grow best there now, and your farm if you have one) and what you can do: fly there, or fly there and start a farm. Previous and Next step through every destination, and the Your farms buttons jump to each farm.

  • Fly to one of your farms, or to a new planet to buy a farm there (each farm has its own robots, sheds and storage).
  • The hold carries goods and seeds between farms. Load at a farm in the Travel menu's Cargo tab; unloading needs the matching shed and room in it. Illegal cargo in the hold counts in every farm's inspection.
  • Money, the loan, the calendar and the Planet Hopper are shared by all farms.

Remote Relay Station

A building (20,000 nibs) that links its farm to the Command Center Chair in your Personal Space Base. The relay list is only in the base: the chair lists every farm you own with its crops, goods, water, thirsty and infested plants, weeds, helpers and strikes, and Connect takes control of any farm with a relay at once (no night passes and the clock is shared). While connected, press R (or the Base button) to return to your Personal Space Base. You stay at the farm with the Planet Hopper, so flying and loading cargo wait until you return; anything that starts a flight returns you first.

Space stations

Stations have no farm, only a market that buys from the hold in bulk. Each day their capacity refills and each category's price drifts by up to ±10%.

StationPaysBuys per dayLawsNotes

Breakdowns and repairs

Robots break down at random while they work. Every bit of wear a job or a move adds carries a chance:

chance = 0.003 × wear added × (1 + current wear ÷ 25)

A fresh Farmoton breaks down about once in 1,300 jobs; at 50% wear, about once in 500 (moves count for a fifth of a job). Helpers wear more slowly, so they break less often. Robots never break on farms you are away from, and idle robots never break.

A broken robot does nothing until it is fixed: the Farmoton will not drive or use tools, and helpers and the autopilot stop. Press B (or the red wrench) to fix it yourself with the puzzle for its fault, or pay the mechanic 800 nibs to fix it at once. A puzzle you leave stays the same until you come back to it.

FaultPuzzle
Mechanical: a jammed gearA gearbox of steel plates on a 6 × 6 grid. Plates slide only along their length; free the gold gear and slide it out through the gap on the right. There are 10 layouts, from 8 to 21 moves.
Hydraulic: a broken lineA 6 × 5 rack of hose sections. Turn them so pressure flows from the pump to the outlet valve; pressurized hoses turn blue.
Electrical: burned-out partsA schematic of 4 branches. Each number sits on a component, and the wires between them carry + − × ÷. A branch's end part needs the value the branch works out to, doing × and ÷ before + and −. Some branches are fed the answer of the branch above by a blue wire, so that one comes first. A wrong part burns out another.

Visiting robots

Special robots roll in from the right along the bottom of the farm screen, and now and then a person walks in. The clock pauses while they talk.

VisitorWhenWhat it does
Surplusoton (dark gold)About every 30 days: day 30, 60, 90… moved a day early or late at random for each farmOffers to buy every legal good in the sheds and trailers for one price: half their base value (the game never says this). It leaves contraband alone. You accept or decline; the planet's people like to see a farmer turn it away.
Dealoton (coral, lilac box)Every 10–20 days on each farm, a new random wait after each visit (if you're elsewhere when it's due, it comes on your next day there)Names one good chosen at random from every legal crop and animal material in the game, whether you have any or not, and a price per unit of 1.5–3× its base price. If you have some, it offers to buy every unit in your sheds and trailers at that price; otherwise it tells you what you missed and leaves.
Weatheroton (teal)When a season starts, or on your first visit to a farm during a season you haven't seen thereGives the outlook for the rest of the season (temperature and daylight ranges, humidity, rain) and the four crops that suit it best on average.
Liaisonoton (blue-gray with a tilted track, blue box)Day 4 on each farm (counting the day you arrive as day 1) to introduce itself. If you say no, it comes back with a new request every 90–180 days. Once you agree, it comes each time you fill a request, bringing the next.Speaks for the planet's local government. A request is 3 different legal crops, 10–30 of each, picked from the better-suited half of crops on that planet over its year. It pays minimum market value (0.9× base price) and takes only the amounts asked. Deliver through the Planet Representative in the space port, a crop at a time and in part if you like; goods come from the sheds and trailers. A regrowing crop stays on the requests for at least 3 in a row. Each planet keeps its own agreement; the tab also shows requests filled and nibs paid there. It also brings the planet's appeals for donations, at least 45 days apart.
Industroton (sooty orange, orange box)Once for each building below on every farm, on that farm's own days (day 1 is the day you arrive): the Industrial Waste Incinerator around day 18–22; the Small Robot Factory around day 45–55; the Containment Facility around day 90–110; the Farmoton Assembly Plant around day 200–210.Offers rent for putting an industrial building in the far corner of your farm, off the plot. Accept and it goes up at once, moving anything in its way; it can't be moved or removed. Each pays its rent at night on its days: Industrial Waste Incinerator (2×2 tiles), 100 nibs every 10 days; Small Robot Factory (4×4 tiles), 200 nibs every 10 days; Containment Facility (8×4 tiles), 250 nibs every 12 days; Farmoton Assembly Plant (12×6 tiles), 500 nibs every 15 days. The planet's people dislike industry on their farmland, and they like it less with every payment. Upset them enough and some will steal animals and sabotage robots overnight, and in the end the local government stops buying from you. Keep them furious for months on end and they start burning your buildings down, and in time they drive you off the planet. You can't farm there for 90 days, and then a farm there costs double, doubling each time. Keep them happy, through donations, and they may weed or clear pests for you in the night.
Kyrn (a man in a suit)Once, 3 days after you have both sold a Farmoton and hired a farm hand (in either order, on any farms)A representative of the local government, who offers to speak to you instead of the Liaisonoton. Say yes and he brings every planet's requests and appeals in its place from then on; nothing else about them changes.
Smuggler (a man in a hat with a satchel)Every 20–45 days on each farm, a new random wait after each visitOffers 5–15 of one illegal good at a price per unit a little under its base price (it never says how much). You buy them all, or as many as fit in that good's shed, or send him away. Smuggling traders at the market may pay more for them; just remember they are contraband.
Barx (a green alien in a straw hat and overalls)Once you own 5 farms, to invite you to the farming coalition (again every 60 days if you say no); then with each new request, a seat on the board, and the board's motionsSee The farming coalition below.
Jymo (a purple alien in a sharp suit)Once you own 10 farms, to sell you the Void Yacht. If you have no Personal Space Base yet, his first offer is one of his own for 100,000 nibs ("Maybe later" brings him back with it every 15 days, or as soon as you can afford it), and the yacht comes on his next visit. Say "Maybe later" to the yacht and he comes back every 15 days, or as soon as you can afford it. Once that is settled, every 25–45 days with a luxurySells luxuries for your Personal Space Base: see The Void Yacht and Jymo's luxuries.
Tactiton (olive green with a gold star), or once you've chosen Kyrn an officer in uniform from the planet's alliance: General Perpesis (Deimos Alliance), General Libaad (Enceladus Pact), Colonel Ovtroof (Io Union), Major Settbach (Teegarden Collective), General Eizzeng (Tethys Coalition), Captain Ibveus (Titan Mining Corporation), Corporal Punn (Vesta Conclave)Each autumn on a farm, once you've farmed there 45 daysAsks, for the planet's military, for 15–40 of one of the 4 legal crops that suit the season best. Give it now, or agree and it's collected overnight once the farm has it all (managers keep it back for them); it pays nothing. Your workers don't like it and every planet thinks a little less of you, but the planet's alliance and its allies are pleased, and its enemies and everyone else are not. See Alliances.
Historoton (parchment brown with spectacles), or Eresom S. Tree once you've chosen KyrnEvery 20–60 days on each farm, a new random wait after each visitIntroduces itself, then tells you a fact about the galaxy's history each visit, in order, starting over once it has told them all.
Ashley Z. Selzpetch (a woman in a blue suit)On each farm once you've farmed there 60 days; turned down, again every 60–90 days, and 160 days after a canceled dealOffers Robototon Corporation's produce program. See Alliances.
Alliance liaison (a woman with a sash and clipboard; each planet's office has its own)Every 20–50 days on each farm, a new random wait after each visitAsks for a donation to the planet's alliance: 2,500, 5,000, 7,500, 10,000 nibs, or nothing. See Alliances.

Visitors only come to the farm you are on, and not while you are at a station.

The farming coalition

Once you own 5 farms, Barx invites you to join the farming coalition. Members pay 10% less for farming supplies: seeds, water delivery, pesticide and Animal Feed, and managers buying for you pay the same. In return the coalition asks for crops: a request is 3 legal crops that suit the farm you are on, 15–40 of each. There's nothing to deliver: overnight, the coalition collects each crop from whichever farm has the whole amount in its sheds and trailers, and pays minimum market value. When every crop is in, Barx brings the next request. The Planet Representative in the space port shows the request and how long you have left.

Go 60 days without a crop collected and you're thrown out, for good (the night report warns you in the last 10 days). Managers leave what the coalition still needs in the sheds instead of selling it or giving it away.

After 90 days as a member Barx offers you a seat on the board. Turn it down and he asks once more, 180 days later. Board members vote on motions Barx brings every 20–40 days, each about a different part of the galaxy:

MotionVote yesVote no
Forgive the debts of new farmers leasing land in a struggling areaCosts 1,000 nibs; the people of every planet think better of youThe coalition thinks better of you
Build food distribution centers in a hard-to-reach areaCosts 2,000 nibs; every planet thinks better of youEvery planet thinks worse of you
Send a major food package to a disaster zoneThe coalition's next 10 requests ask for double; every planet thinks better of youEvery planet thinks worse of you

Alliances

Every planet belongs to one of 7 alliances. The Great Conflict ended over a hundred years ago, but the grudge wars between them go on. What an alliance thinks of you is what the people of its planets think of you (see the Industroton's entry in Visiting robots for what that does), so pleasing one alliance pleases every planet in it, and its allies too, while its enemies take it badly. Each alliance names its own allies and enemies; they don't always agree, and only an alliance's direct allies and enemies count, never their friends' friends. The planet table in Planets and the travel map show which alliance each planet is in.

The military

Each autumn the planet's military asks for a crop in season. Giving it (now, or collected overnight once you have it all) changes what each alliance thinks of you: the planet's own alliance +0.75, its allies +0.25, its enemies -0.75 and every other alliance -0.5, on top of -0.1 for every planet. Each of your workers on that farm is a little less happy (-0.25). Refusing changes nothing.

Alliance liaisons

Each planet's alliance office asks for a donation now and then. Every 2,500 nibs you give counts once: the alliance thinks +1 better of you, its enemies -1, and every other alliance, allies included, -0.25; the planet's people +0.1 more and each worker on the farm +0.1. So 10,000 nibs counts four times over. Nothing happens if you give nothing.

Robototon Corporation's produce program

Ashley Z. Selzpetch offers it on each farm, and asks again 60–90 days after you turn her down. Accept and Robototon replaces every crop shed there with a Refrigerated Warehouse that holds 5,000 goods of any kind (what was in the sheds moves in). At the start of every winter on that planet, Roboton Mostly Sustenance empties it of every legal good and pays 20% of their base price; contraband stays. You can still sell at the market, but Roboton expects at least 200 goods each winter: if the farm grew that many since the last pickup (harvests and animal goods) and fewer are left in the warehouse, Roboton cancels the deal on that planet, takes the warehouse away and puts back the sheds it replaced, at their old storage levels. A poor season that grew fewer than 200 never counts against you. After a cancellation she offers the deal there again 160 days later; your deals on other planets carry on. Some workers like the deal and some don't (those who like robots are more often pleased), and they feel the same way at every pickup. Every planet thinks less of you (-0.5 when you accept, -0.1 each pickup), and the alliances feel differently about it:

AllianceOn acceptingEach winter pickup
Deimos Alliance+1+0.25
Enceladus Pact+0.25+0.05
Io Union+0.5+0.1
Teegarden Collective-0.25-0.05
Tethys Coalition-0.5-0.1
Titan Mining Corporation+1+0.25
Vesta Conclave-1-0.25

Some alliances weigh things their own way. On the planets of the Titan Mining Corporation and the Deimos Alliance, nobody minds your industrial or commercial dealings (the Industroton's buildings and rent, Roboton's deal and pickups, selling to the Surplusoton): those never change what those planets think of you. While you have Roboton's deal on any farm, the Titan Mining Corporation thinks a little better of you every night (+0.1). On the planets of the Teegarden Collective and the Tethys Coalition, the good your humanitarian acts do (donations, food drives, gifts to the alliance, the coalition's relief motions) counts 1.2× with the planet and with those alliances.

The people of a planet's space port show what they think of you. Where you're disliked (opinion -25 or lower) they hurry away and won't tell you anything. Where you're adored (75 or higher) some come up to you with a gift: a handful of nibs, seeds of whatever suits the farm best that day, or just their thanks.

Opinions run from -100 to 100 and the game never shows them; workers' moods run from 0 to 100.

Milestones and your Personal Space Base

The Interplanetary Growers Alliance (IGA) rewards farmers who keep producing food. It can't pay cash, so each milestone gives something for your Personal Space Base (PSB). Milestones count every farm you own, are checked whenever anything changes, and once reached stay reached. The Tipoton announces each one. The trophy button on the bottom bar, right of the seed and status buttons (or L), lists them all with their rewards, ticking each one off with the day you reached it.

MilestoneGoalReward
Livestock KeeperBuild an Animal Barn on any farm.An aquarium for your Personal Space Base, with two fish to start.
Local HireHire a farm hand.A workshop room for your Personal Space Base.
Trusted DeputyHire a farm manager.A lounge for your Personal Space Base.
A Roof OverheadBuild a garage on any farm.Keys to a small Personal Space Base.
Extra HandsBuy your first helper robot.An awards case for your Personal Space Base, to keep your IGA medals in.
LiftoffBuy the Planet Hopper.A 5×5 rocket rug for your Personal Space Base.
Bigger HoldUpgrade the Planet Hopper's cargo hold.A furniture kit for your Personal Space Base.
Management MaterialBuy a Manager Robot.A new 7×9 room for your Personal Space Base.
Two WorldsStart a second farm.A Command Center Chair for your Personal Space Base. Sit in it to take control of any farm with a Remote Relay Station.

Awards

The IGA also gives awards: medals for farming well, with no base reward. The Tipoton delivers each one, and their medals sit in the awards case. The Awards tab of the milestones screen shows how close you are to each.

AwardHow to earn it
Admirable HumanoidatarianKeep a farm's whole staff happy for a long time.
Interplanetary LegendComplete 10 Planet Local requests on each of 4 planets.
Kindest HeartGive your surplus food to a planet's food drive 10 times.
Local LegendComplete 10 Planet Local requests on the same planet.
Pest Free FarmerEnd five days in a row with crops growing and no pests on any of your farms.
Prolific PlanterStart farms on 5 planets.

Pest Free Farmer counts nights: a night counts if crops are growing on any farm and none has pests; any pest starts the count again, and a night with nothing growing anywhere neither counts nor breaks it. Prolific Planter counts every farm you have started, including any lost since.

The base

The base is in orbit and comes with its own mini-shuttle from the planet; when you fly to another planet, the Planet Hopper tows it along. Once you have it, the Base button next to the milestones button (or K) takes you there from any farm; no time passes while you are there, and leaving brings you back. It is seen from above with everything outside it black: at first a 7×7 room joined by a single door tile to a 7×5 room, each with its own floor color, and later a 7×9 room below the first. There is no one to walk around: click the aquarium, the awards case or the Command Center Chair (or use the buttons along the top) to use them. The rocket rug and the furniture kit's sofa, bed, table, shelves, lamps and plants are for show.

  • Awards case: shows the medal for every award earned, with empty places for the rest.
  • Command Center Chair: opens the relay list, so you can take control of any farm with a Remote Relay Station.

The aquarium

It comes with 2 fish and a few decorations. Feed them in the aquarium screen: once more than 14 days pass without food they all die (the night report warns you the morning before). Dead fish lie on the sand until you clear them out. Up to 12 fish and 10 decorations fit; fish bought into an empty tank arrive fed.

In the base you walk about with the arrow keys or W A S D. Face the aquarium, awards case or Command Center Chair and press Space to use it (or click it). 7, the Move key, picks up the furniture in front of you and puts it down again wherever it fits inside a room; Esc puts it back. Time runs on at half speed while you are in the base, with the day and time on its top bar, and your farms keep working; if midnight passes, the night report appears there.

The base's Store button sells furniture (an armchair, bean bag, desk, telescope and planet globe), a workbench for practicing the repair puzzles whenever you like (each kind of fault needs its own practice kit, sold there too), and an arcade cabinets, each keeping your best score: Space Snake, Shapey Blocks (turn and drop falling shapes to fill whole rows) and Swap-n-Match (swap neighboring gems to line up three or more of a color, with a limited number of swaps a game). What you buy appears in a free spot in the base. The clock keeps running while you play any arcade cabinet, in the base, the yacht or a utility shack.

The Void Yacht and Jymo's luxuries

Jymo of the Deluxe Luxury Company sells the Void Yacht for 200,000 nibs. It docks at your base: a Void Yacht button on the base's top bar takes you aboard, and a Personal Space Base button takes you back. It's shaped like a boat, with a sun deck, a grand saloon, a games room and a bow lounge, and you walk about and move furniture just as in the base. Its own Store sells different furniture and three cabinets you won't find in the base:

PiecePrice
Asteroid Belt cabinet12,000Steer, thrust and blast the asteroids before they hit you.
Cocktail bar14,000Polished, well stocked and lit from beneath.
Hot tub22,000Always warm, always bubbling.
Sun lounger6,000For basking in the light of whichever star is nearest.
Moon Maze cabinet10,000Find the way out of each maze before the clock runs down.
Minesweeper cabinet10,000Uncover every safe square of the field without setting off a mine.
Potted palm4,000A touch of the tropics, in a gold pot.
Grand piano30,000Glossy, black and perfectly in tune.
Star projector16,000Casts the constellations of home across the floor.
  • Minesweeper: uncover every safe square without hitting a mine. Click or Space to uncover, right-click or F to flag.
  • Moon Maze: reach each maze's exit before the clock runs out; every maze cleared adds time, and the mazes grow.
  • Asteroid Belt: left and right turn, up thrusts, Space fires. Shots break big asteroids into smaller ones.

Once the yacht is settled (bought or turned down), Jymo comes back now and then with a luxury for the base or the yacht:

LuxuryPriceSize
Beef Beetle Shell Rug20,0003×3 tiles

The rugs come in a different pattern (Beef Beetle shell) or color (Woolbug wool) each time, and you can own as many as you like; there's only one goat. If you own the yacht, choose where it goes when you buy it. Later, pick it up with 7 and press Space to send it across. Not everyone admires this kind of spending: buying the yacht or the goat makes the people of every planet think less of you.

On screen

  • Top bar: the planet; the day, time, sun (tinted the planet's sun color; a moon at night) and hours of daylight, season, temperature, humidity and a rain cloud when raining; then your nibs, the Farmoton's battery (a bolt while charging at the garage) and onboard water, and a red warning with your debt and strikes.
  • Bottom bar: the tools 1–7, the seed selector with ⓘ for the seed's details and a button to show or hide the status pane, then the menus as icons with their keys. Every icon names itself when you hover it.
  • Bottom right: what the Farmoton is facing or carrying, and the status pane (hopper, trailer, tank, pesticide, animals, wear, autopilot, helpers).

Music and credits

Quiet background music plays on the farm (Comfortable Mystery 2, Lasting Hope, Serene, Trio for Piano, Cello, and Clarinet, Magic Forest, and Virtutes Vocis) and in your Personal Space Base (Floating Cities, Unpromised, and String Impromptu Number 1), in a shuffled order. The title, story, planet choice and stations are silent. Switch music on or off with the note button left of the seed selector on the bottom bar, or in the pause menu; the choice is remembered. Buttons, menus, tabs, errors, robot messages and milestones have short interface sounds, and the robots make sounds as they work (plowing, planting, cutting, harvesting, unloading, moving buildings, breaking down and being repaired), heard from where they are on the farm, with a motor hum while they drive. Animals make a quiet call of their own kind every so often. Switch all sounds off with Sounds in the pause menu. Credits, on the title screen and in the pause menu, name the art (Game Art by Kenney.nl) and the music (Kevin MacLeod, incompetech.com, under Creative Commons: By Attribution 4.0).

Saving

  • The game autosaves after every night and every flight, and when you quit to the title or close the window. F5 saves at any time.
  • Load Game on the title screen continues from the last save.
